Dilīpa
------------------------------------------
Dilīpa was a great king of the Sūryavaṁśa (the royal race which traced its origin from सूर्य or the Sun-god) and the ड़थेर् of रघु who became even more renowned than his ड़थेर्. In fact, the race itself came to be known as ‘Raghuvaṁśa’ after him.
Dilīpa had no children. As per the directions of his (royal) preceptor वसिष्ठ, he faithfully served his cow Nandinī (an offspring of the famous कामधेनु, the celestial cow) who tested him by creating a critical situation. दिलीप came out victorious and was then blessed by the divine cow. As a result, he got a valiant son whom he named ‘Raghu’.
Dilīpa was also known as खट्वाङ्ग. He was once requested by the gods in हेअवेन् to help them in their fight against the demons. With his valiant assistance they attained victory. When they offered him a boon, he just asked them to know how much of his life was still left. On getting the reply ‘one मुहूर्त’ (about 48 minutes) he immediately sat in meditation, concentrated his मिन्द् on Lord विष्णु and gave up the body, thus attaining मुक्ति or लिबेरतिओन्.
